messages:
Alex Chen: FYI ACME bank POC — hitting an auth/roles blocker for streaming SDK + function calls. Root token works for normal requests but streaming sessions lose delegated roles. Anyone seen this?

Maria Gomez: Oof. Is this when you do role-delegation via header + session-token? Example?

Alex Chen: Yeah. We set X-Role-Delegation: acme_admin and exchange to ephemeral creds with /v1/auth/delegate. Streaming connect uses websocket url: wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-2

Jordan Patel: Quick question: are you using session cookies or short-lived bearer? We expect short-lived bearer in Authorization header for SSE/ws. Cookies/Set-Cookie on upgrade can be dropped by some proxies. :thinking:

Alex Chen: Using bearer. Token example:
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJ...delegation_id=abcd
X-Role-Delegation: acme_admin
```
But after ~30s the server returns tool call errors: "403 role not authorized for tool"

Priya Rao: @Alex can you paste the security questionnaire item? We might need SCIM group mappings and KMS attestations for tool calls. Also need to confirm that delegated role is included in the token's claims (roles/allowed_tools).

Alex Chen: Here's the relevant snippet from their security doc: "Delegated tokens must include roles array and be signed by upstream IdP; Redwood must accept federated roles via JWT assertion or via OIDC token exchange."

Maria Gomez: On pricing: ACME asked about cost delta if they use Dedicated vs Hosted for streaming-heavy workload (lots of function/tool calls). Short answer: Dedicated reduces per-token cost for heavy sustained throughput and gives predictable tail-latency SLA — I can pull numbers.

Jordan Patel: For the function/tool calling issue: tool authorization is enforced per model/process that executes the tool. If the delegated role isn't propagated to the runtime instance handling the function, it will 403. Could be routing/fanout issue. Do you see logs with different trace ids?

Alex Chen: I can share logs. Sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c. Logs show upstream token accepted at auth service, but a downstream internal call to tool-runner lacks role in header.

Priya Rao: That sounds like a header strip in the proxy between runtime and tool-runner. We need to confirm internal header passthrough config. Also confirm KMS key policy for tool-runner allows role-based access.

Onboarding Bot: Link to internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/presales/streaming-role-delegation

Maria Gomez: Plan: Alex to gather traces + minimal repro (curl or small node snippet). Jordan to check runtime header propagation rules. Priya to review security questionnaire and confirm SCIM/KMS gaps. I'll prepare cost delta bullets for sales call Wednesday.

Alex Chen: Will do. Minimal repro: node ws connect + Authorization header + X-Role-Delegation. I'll post snippet here.

Jordan Patel: If you can include a tiny repro we can try to reproduce on staging. Also list whether they use on-prem IdP or cloud (SAML, OIDC).

Alex Chen: They use on-prem ADFS (SAML) with a federation to OIDC. Might be why JWT roles not in standard place.

Priya Rao: Ok. Could be missing claim mapping during SAML->OIDC exchange. I'll circulate a list of claims we require.

Maria Gomez: Thanks everyone — will sync after Alex posts repro. :thumbsup:
